summary.text: Green grape immortal essence is the immortal essence of rank six Gu Immortals, stored as beads and spent to feed Immortal Gu or fuel immortal methods.

claims.text: In Hu Immortal blessed land, abundant immortal essence fills an enormous golden bowl. Most of it has congealed into balls that look like grapes. The text names this store as something only rank six Gu Immortals have: green grape immortal essence. Each pearl holds far more immortal essence than the store in the three kings blessed land.

Fang Yuan counts seventy-eight pieces of green grape immortal essence in the golden bowl, plus a layer of blue-green immortal liquid essence at the bottom, amounting to seventy-eight and a half. One bead feeds Fixed Immortal Travel Gu: the Immortal Gu lands on the bead, consumes it, and after that feeding does not need food for about six years.

Hu Immortal blessed land holds only seventy-eight beads. After one bead feeds Fixed Immortal Travel and two more teleport a swamp crab, the land spirit reports the cost. Because Hu Immortal is already dead, these green grape immortal essence beads cannot be replenished; each bead used is one less for later.

When Fang Yuan wills a bead of green grape immortal essence into his strength path immortal aperture, it spreads through the blessed land and turns into almost limitless primeval essence. From that point he can use mortal Gu without worrying about primeval essence expenditure. The text marks this as the biggest difference between mortal and immortal.

Gu Immortals at rank six have green grape immortal essence. They face an earthly calamity every ten years and a heavenly tribulation every one hundred years. After three hundred years and three heavenly tribulations, they become rank seven. Gu Immortals at rank seven have red date immortal essence. Immortal apertures at rank eight create white litchi immortal essence.
Rank scale sits on ranks and realms.
